text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your vertigo, can you describe exactly when the spinning sensation started and if it is constant or comes in episodes? Also, are you experiencing any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice if any specific head movement, such as rolling over in bed, triggered the spinning sensation? Also, have you experienced any recent head trauma or viral illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: To further evaluate your symptoms, I would like to see if there are any objective signs of vestibular dysfunction. REQUEST TEST: Head_Impulse_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the head impulse test was normal, this suggests a central cause rather than a peripheral one like vestibular neuritis. Do you have any history of stroke risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol, and are you currently experiencing any other neurological symptoms like difficulty speaking, double vision, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty with coordination, such as trouble walking in a straight line, or do you have any double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your arms or legs? I need to rule out a central cause like a cerebellar stroke given your age and the sudden onset.
